historic_survey.style: Folk Victorian, with Gothic Revival bargeboard
historic_survey.note: The Hittell House, called perhaps the most expressive known Folk Victorian in San Francisco: a ground-floor full-facade front porch, front-facing gable, symmetrical facade and jig-sawn cut trim, with decorative bargeboard along each side eave that belongs more to Gothic Revival. It could be found eligible under Criterion C/3.

historical_record.description: Built as a Folk Victorian dwelling — a vernacular wood-frame house set with its long side parallel to the street, under a steeply pitched side-facing gable roof, with a porch running the length of the façade and little decorative trim beyond brackets and window hoods. The type is rare in San Francisco, where most such houses were pulled down for later development or lost in 1906. The house is associated with the Hittell family.
